content: The following individuals, representing various organizations and institutions, participated in discussions and initiatives related to leprosy and global health: Ms. Mondie Tharp, serving as the Project Manager for the Global Partnership for Zero Leprosy, is based in Decatur, Georgia, United States. Dr. Arielle Cavaliero, the Global Business Director for the Leprosy Flagship under Global Health and Corporate Responsibility at Novartis AG, is located in Basel, Switzerland. Professor Takahiro Nanri, the Executive Director of the Sasakawa Health Foundation, operates out of Tokyo, Japan. Ms. Aya Tobiki, the Chief Program Officer for the Hansen’s Disease Program at the Sasakawa Health Foundation, is also based in Tokyo, Japan. Ms. Kiyomi Takahashi, the Program Director for the Hansen’s Disease Program at the Sasakawa Health Foundation, works in Tokyo, Japan. Mr. Geoff Warne, the Chief Executive Officer of the International Federation of Anti-Leprosy Associations, is located in Cointrin, Switzerland. Additional participants included: Dr. Vijay Kumar Pannikar, based in Hosuru, Karnataka, India, and Dr. Rajan Babu Karigiri, from Tamil Nadu, India, who attended in person. Professor Jan Hendrik Richardus and Dr. David Blok, both from the Erasmus Medical Centre in Rotterdam, The Netherlands, participated remotely. Professor Paul Fine, affiliated with the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom, joined remotely. Dr. Epco Hasker, from the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, also participated remotely. Dr. Peter Steinmann, representing the Swiss Tropical and Public Health Institute in Basel, Switzerland, contributed remotely. Professor Annemieke Geluk, from Leiden University in Leiden, The Netherlands, participated remotely. Ms. Christine Fenenga, a consultant in global health inclusive, based in Amsterdam, The Netherlands, joined remotely. Representatives from the World Health Organization (WHO) included: Dr. Erwin Cooreman, the Team Leader for the Global Leprosy Programme at the WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia, attended in person. Dr. VRR Pemmaraju, a Technical Officer for the Global Leprosy Programme at the WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia, also participated in person.
